products.name: Freepik AI
products.note: Stock image AI generation; commercial licensing; EU-hosted; content moderation

reading.body:
Freepik sells AI image generation as a licensed stock product, hosted in the EU, with content moderation built in.

The product is positioned as a commercial licensing business rather than a model developer. The note attached to it names the things a buyer of generated images actually needs: rights to use the output, a jurisdiction where the data sits, and a moderation layer that keeps the output sellable. That is a distribution and compliance story, not a training or compute story.

For AI specifically, this is the downstream end of the pipeline. Image generation at this layer competes on licensing terms, hosting location, and moderation policy, all of which are decided well above the GPU. Nothing in the data describes model size, training runs, inference volume, or where the compute comes from, so no claim can be made about Freepik's power or data center footprint.

The record is thin in a specific way. It gives one product, one category, one website, and a set of descriptive tags, with no dates, no figures, no partners, and no infrastructure detail. It establishes what Freepik sells and where it says it hosts, and it does not establish how much compute that requires or who supplies it.
